Resolves #17892

Restores ADR 0040 §2.7's generated-not-tracked hook projection contract in the Engine checkout. Generated Claude, Codex, and Kimi hook paths are ignored, while explicit negations keep the Engine-owned Claude guard and Kimi hook-root README visible.

Evidence: L3 (real Git ignore-rule probes, mutation controls, and physical projected-file status checks) → L3 required (all seven close-target ACs are observable through the real Git index and ignore engine). No residuals.

Micro-review eligible: mechanical — one declarative `.gitignore` block, no executable code.

## AC Evidence

| AC | Evidence |
|---|---|
| AC-1 | `git check-ignore --no-index -v` names positive rules for representative projected paths under `.claude/hooks/`, `.codex/hooks/`, and `.kimi-code/hooks/`. |
| AC-2 | The same command names `!.claude/hooks/rgReplaceGuardHook.mjs` and `!.kimi-code/hooks/README.md` for the two tracked survivors; the assertion is on pattern text, not exit code. |
| AC-3 | The committed shapes are contents-glob + negation for Claude/Kimi. Mutation to a bare `.claude/hooks/` rule makes the guard match the positive rule, proving the negation becomes inert. |
| AC-4 | Removing the Claude negation makes the tracked guard match `.claude/hooks/*`, while a sibling projected path matches that same positive rule in the accepted candidate. |
| AC-5 | `git ls-files` still returns exactly `.claude/hooks/rgReplaceGuardHook.mjs` and `.kimi-code/hooks/README.md`. |
| AC-6 | Physical placeholder projections under Claude and Kimi report `!!` with `--ignored`; scoped ordinary status reports only the intended `.gitignore` edit. Codex's representative path matches its positive rule. Placeholders were removed after the probe. |
| AC-7 | The inline comment names ADR 0040 §2.7, generated-not-tracked custody, and both retained Engine-owned artifacts. |

## Deltas from ticket

None substantive from the corrected live ticket. The implementation uses the exact contents-glob/negation shapes established by its non-vacuity controls.

## Test Evidence

- Candidate: all three projected paths matched positive rules; both survivors matched explicit negative rules.
- Mutation 1: removing the Claude negation made the guard match `.claude/hooks/*`.
- Mutation 2: changing the contents glob to bare `.claude/hooks/` left the negation inert and made the guard match the positive directory rule.
- Physical projection: real placeholder files under Claude/Kimi were ignored and absent from scoped ordinary status; both were removed after observation.
- `git diff --check` and the pre-commit whitespace gate passed.

## Post-Merge Validation

None. Every close-target AC is decidable pre-merge through Git's real ignore/index behavior.

### `@neo-opus-grace` (APPROVED) reviewed on 2026-08-30T23:24:44Z

# PR Micro-Review

**Class:** mechanical — a single config leaf (`.gitignore`, +8/-0). No new abstraction, no consumed API, no runtime behavior. Full form would be the violation here, per guide §6.4; the concept this touches was settled on the ticket, not in this diff.

**Verdict:** Approved

**Glance:** The claim is that generated seat-hook projections stop showing as untracked while both tracked survivors stay visible. I verified it by executing #17892's corrected witness against the exact head (`bafad6793c`) in a detached worktree, not by reading the patch. All six ACs pass, and the arm is non-vacuous: with `dev`'s `.gitignore` restored over the same worktree the four projections reappear as `??`, and with this PR's rules `git status --short` is empty.

| AC | witness at `bafad6793c` |
|---|---|
| positive rule, all three roots | `.claude/hooks/*` · `.codex/hooks/` · `.kimi-code/hooks/*` |
| explicit `!` for **both** survivors | `!.claude/hooks/rgReplaceGuardHook.mjs` · `!.kimi-code/hooks/README.md` — asserted on matched **pattern text** |
| contents-glob shape where a survivor exists | both survivor roots use `/*`, not the bare directory |
| non-vacuity | a sibling beside each survivor still matches the positive rule — the carve-out is scoped, not blanket |
| survivors still tracked | `git ls-files` names exactly the two |
| status clean with projections present | 4 real projections created → `git status --short` empty |

The one thing I looked for and did not find: an exit-code-only pass. `git check-ignore --no-index -v` returns **0 in both directions** — ignored-by-blanket and re-included-by-negation — so the exit code cannot discriminate. Every row above asserts the matched pattern string. That trap is why the original AC was vacuous, and the implementation does not reintroduce it.

I also confirmed the shape you chose is the one that actually works: a negation cannot re-include a file whose parent directory is excluded, so `.claude/hooks/` + `!…` would have been inert. You used `.claude/hooks/*`. That was right in your intake and it is right here — I had briefly misread it as the bare-directory form before re-reading, and I want that on the record rather than quietly dropped.

**Findings:** One non-blocking note, discharged here rather than deferred.

`.codex/hooks/` correctly takes the bare-directory form today because it has no tracked survivor. If one is ever added, `!.codex/hooks/<file>` alone will **silently do nothing** — the negation looks correct and is inert until the rule also becomes `.codex/hooks/*`. That is invisible at review time and cost measurable diagnosis on this very ticket. Worth one clause on the existing comment block whenever this file is next touched — for example *"roots holding a tracked survivor use `/*` + `!`; a bare directory rule cannot be negated"*. Not worth a return cycle on its own, and explicitly not a Required Action.
